    AI Overview
    The 152nd Kentucky Derby is scheduled for
    Saturday, May 2, 2026, at Churchill Downs in Louisville, KY, with gates opening at 9 a.m. ET. As of early April 2026, Renegade is considered a top favorite after winning the Arkansas Derby, with Commandment and Danon Bourbon also emerging as major contenders. 
    Key 2026 Kentucky Derby Details: 
    • Date: Saturday, May 2, 2026.
    • Location: Churchill Downs, Louisville, KY.
    • Key Prep Races: Arkansas Derby (Renegade), Florida Derby (Commandment), UAE Derby (Wonder Dean).
    • Top Contenders (Early April 2026): Renegade (4-length Arkansas Derby winner), Commandment (Florida Derby winner), Danon Bourbon (Undefeated Japan-based runner).
    • Tickets & Packages: Official 2-day ticket packages and premium dining options are available through Derby Experiences and Ticketmaster. 
    Current Top Horses & Storylines 
    • Renegade: Marked as the 7-2 favorite in early April after an impressive Arkansas Derby victory.
    • Commandment: A top contender (9-2) coming off a Florida Derby win, managed by trainer Brad Cox and owner Wathnan Racing.
    • Danon Bourbon: A perfect 3-for-3 Japanese-based horse considered a serious threat.
    • Injuries: Early favorite Paladin is sidelined with a right front ankle injury. 
    Event Schedule 
    • Kentucky Oaks: Friday, May 1, 2026.
    • Kentucky Derby: Saturday, May 2, 2026 (First race 11:00 a.m. ET). 
    Note: The final Kentucky Derby futures pool closes April 4, 2026.

    AI Overview
    The 152nd Kentucky Derby will take place on Saturday, May 2, 2026, at Churchill Downs in Louisville, KY, with gates opening at 9 a.m. ET and first post at 11 a.m. ET. The main Kentucky Derby race is scheduled for 6:57 p.m. ET. Derby Week features events from Saturday, April 25, through Saturday, May 2. 
    Key 2026 Kentucky Derby Week Schedule (April 25 – May 2) 
    • Saturday, April 25 (Opening Day): Gates open 11:30 a.m., First Post 12:45 p.m. 
    • Sunday, April 26 (Sunday Funday): Gates open 11:30 a.m., First Post 12:45 p.m. 
    • Monday, April 27 (Dawn at the Downs): Gates open 7 a.m. for morning workouts.
    • Tuesday, April 28 (502'sDay): Gates open 11:30 a.m., First Post 12:45 p.m. 
    • Wednesday, April 29 (Derby Week's Winsday): Gates open 11:30 a.m., First Post 12:45 p.m. 
    • Thursday, April 30 (Thurby): Gates open 10:30 a.m., First Post 12:45 p.m. 
    • Friday, May 1 (Kentucky Oaks Day): Gates open 11 a.m., First Post 12:30 p.m. 
    • Saturday, May 2 (Kentucky Derby Day): Gates open 9 a.m., First Post 11 a.m. 
    Key Details
    • Main Race: The 152nd Kentucky Derby is the 12th race of the day, with a post time of 6:57 p.m. ET. 
    • Venue: Churchill Downs, Louisville, Kentucky. 
    • Coverage: Typically broadcast on NBC. 
    The week includes the Kentucky Oaks on Friday (a race for 3-year-old fillies) and culminates in the "Run for the Roses" on Saturday.

The 2026 Kentucky Derby takes place on Saturday, May 2 at Churchill Downs, with final prep races and the last futures pool concluding in early April. 
      Key 2026 Kentucky Derby Futures Odds (As of early April 2026): 
      • Paladin: 8-1
      • Chief Wallabee: 8-1
      • Commandment: 12-1
      • Nearly: 12-1

        These odds are from futures pools and subject to significant change based on final prep races like the Blue Grass Stakes.

      • Key Prep Race:
        Further Ado is heavily favored (8-5) in the $1.25 million Blue Grass Stakes at Keeneland on April 4, which is a major final qualifier. 
      • Wild Cards:
        Horses trained by Bob Baffert, such as Brant (priced at 50-1 in some pools), are also being watched closely.

        AI Overview
        Tickets for the 2026 Kentucky Derby (May 2) are on sale now, with prices ranging from roughly $136 for infield general admission to over $1,000–$2,000+ for reserved seating/box seats. Official, all-inclusive 2-day packages frequently range from $2,300 to over $10,000 for luxury, premium, or VIP experiences. 
        Ticket Prices and Options (2026 Season):
        • Infield General Admission: Starts around $136–$196, providing basic access. 
        • Infield Final Turn GA: Starts around $376.50. 
        • Frontside Plaza Walkaround: Starts at roughly $731.85. 
        • Starting Gate Courtyard Reserved: Starts around $1,041. 
        • 1st Floor Clubhouse Boxes: Often range from $1,150–$2,241. 
        • 2-Day Packages (2026): Include food and beverages, ranging from $2,345 (Hampton Inn/Embassy Suites pkg) to $10,000+ for premium clubhouse seating (e.g., Turf Club). 
        Key Considerations:
        • Increased Cost:
          Tickets have seen massive price increases, often rising 231% compared to a decade ago. 
        • Availability:
          Tickets are available through the official Kentucky Derby website](https://www.kentuckyderby.com/seating-experiences/standing-room-general-admission) [4], [Derby Experiences, and official resellers. 
        • Packages:
          Many tickets for the Derby (May 2) and Oaks (May 1) are sold as two-day packages, often including all-inclusive food and alcoholic beverages. 
        Prices are subject to change based on demand and availability.

          Traditions. What are the traditions of the Kentucky Derby 2026?
          About this result

          An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
          AI Overview
          The 2026 Kentucky Derby, running on May 2nd, features iconic, time-honored customs: sipping Mint Juleps, wearing extravagant hats and fascinators, singing "My Old Kentucky Home", and the "Run for the Roses". The "Pink Out" on Oaks Day, Dawn at the Downs, and betting also remain central, iconic festivities. 
          Key Traditions of the Kentucky Derby 2026
          • Mint Juleps: The quintessential bourbon cocktail, often served in commemorative cups. 
          • Derby Hats and Fashion: A display of extravagant, creative headwear, fascinators, and spring fashion for both men and women. 
          • Garland of Roses: The winner is draped in a garland of over 400 roses, earning the race its nickname. 
          • "My Old Kentucky Home": Performed by the Louisville marching band during the post parade. 
          • Kentucky Oaks "Pink Out": Held Friday, May 1st, 2026, where fans wear pink to support breast cancer awareness and the "Lilies for the Fillies". 
          • Dawn at the Downs: Morning workouts allowing fans to watch horses and eat breakfast at Churchill Downs. 
          • Celebrity Watch: High-profile guests appearing on the red carpet. 
          • Culinary Events: The "Taste of Derby" event featuring celebrity chefs. 
          • The Betting Tradition: Heavy wagering on the "fastest two minutes in sports". 
          Synonyms and Similar Terms for Derby Traditions
          • Kentucky Derby Traditions: Derby customs, Derby rituals, signature Derby experiences.
          • Mint Juleps: Bourbon cocktail, signature drink.
          • Derby Hats: Fascinators, ladies' hats, spring headwear, race day fashion.
          • Garland of Roses: Winner's garland, rose blanket.
          • My Old Kentucky Home: Official song, pre-race anthem.
          • Run for the Roses: The Kentucky Derby, the race, the main event.
          All traditions are expected to continue in 2026, following established protocols.

            AI Overview
            The 2026 Kentucky Derby qualifying races (or "prep races" or "Derby trail") consist of a three-part series spanning late 2025 to April 2026, culminating in top-point events like the Blue Grass Stakes, Santa Anita Derby, and Wood Memorial on April 4, 2026. These 100-50-25-15-10 point races are essential for securing a spot in the 20-horse field. 
            Key 2026 Kentucky Derby Prep Races
            • Final Major Preps (100 Points to Winner):
              • UAE Derby: March 28, 2026 
              • Arkansas Derby: Late March 
              • Florida Derby: Late March 
              • Blue Grass Stakes: April 4, 2026 
              • Santa Anita Derby: April 4, 2026 
              • Wood Memorial: April 4, 2026 
            • Prep Season Races (Earlier 2026):
              • Jerome Stakes (Jan 3): Aqueduct 
              • Lecomte Stakes (Jan 17): Fair Grounds 
              • UAE 2000 Guineas (Jan 23): Meydan 
              • Holy Bull Stakes (Jan 31): Gulfstream Park 
              • Withers Stakes (Feb 6): Aqueduct 
              • Southwest Stakes (Feb 6): Oaklawn Park 
              • Sam F. Davis Stakes (Feb 7): Tampa Bay Downs 
              • Risen Star Stakes (Feb 14): Fair Grounds 
              • Saudi Derby (Feb 14): Riyadh 
              • Jeff Ruby Steaks (March): Turfway Park 
            • Other Qualifying Series:
              • Japan Road to the Kentucky Derby: Four specialized races in Japan. 
              • Euro/Mideast Road to the Kentucky Derby: Ten races including the UAE 2000 Guineas, Saudi Derby, and Dubai Road to the Kentucky Derby Stakes (formerly Al Bastakiya). 
            The top point-earners from these events, which also include fall 2025 races like the Iroquois and Breeders' Futurity, qualify for the 152nd Kentucky Derby on May 2, 2026.

              What date is the Kentucky Derby in 2026?
              May 2, 2026
              The Kentucky Derby is held annually on the first Saturday in May. The 152nd running will take place on Saturday, May 2, 2026, with the main race occurring between 6:00 and 7:00 p.m. EST.
